text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland is ready to participate in the risk and duties of Nato member countries as it wishes to join the organisation, Polish president Aleksander Kwasniewski said at a Nato workshop in Prague.
- Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) leader Marian Krzaklewski will run for parliament in Katowice, southern Poland, where he is heading the grouping's list.

AWS is currently torn by conflicts related to forming regional lists of candidates to run in the elections in September. Trade union activists have dominated the lists at the cost of more conservative AWS members, who fear what they call the political block's syndicalist bent.
- The political programme of the centrist Union for Freedom (UW) party allows it to put freedom to a good use, party chairman Leszek Balcerowicz said at the programme's presentation on Sunday.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- The listed food processing and trading firms Farm Food, Sokolow, Animex and Drosed plan to buy other meat plants in an attempt to consolidate the market.
- Poland is lagging behind some Central and East European countries in respect to privatisation, which needs to gather pace, a report by Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique of Paris said.
- The Daewoo Motor Poland (DMP) automotive plant in Lublin will suspend production of the popular Zuk delivery van for the summer. Zuk sales account for 20 percent of DMP's sales.
- The Zanam mining machinery maintenance firm, controlled by the KGHM copper giant, plans to lay off 230 workers, Zanam's trade unions said. The redundancies have been forced by a lack of orders.
- The World Bank may limit financial support for Polish reforms in future due to the country's rapid economic development, a report by the bank said.

- The Expac paper mill in Drezdenko, Gorzow province, has invested 25 million zlotys in a new corrugated cardboard line. The plant will produce 60 million square metres of cardboard annually when the line reaches full output capacity.

- Poland's furniture exports are curbed by a deficit of cheap credits, poor export insurance offer, stable currency exchange rates and unsatisfactory customs services, industry representatives said at a seminar on furniture export opportunities and barriers last Friday.
- The Polfa pharmaceutical plant in Poznan has invested 37.9 million zlotys in facility development in the last two years, the plant's president Zbigniew Bejma said.
- Listed builder Mostostal Zabrze expects to get an infrastructure development contract for the construction of an Isuzu diesel engine plant in Tychy, southern Poland.
- Austria's Ilbau developer has paid $24 million for an 80 percent share stake in the Hotele Warszawskie Syrena hotel chain in Warsaw.
- The listed Forte furniture maker plans to increase its export sales in China from the present $2 million to $6 million in the future, Forte's board member Roman Traczyk said.
- The listed Okocim brewer will launch licensed production of Carlsberg beer to be sold in Poland in summer, the company said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The Kolporter press distribution chain in Kielce is using the delays in the privatisation of the Ruch distribution chain to its own advantage as it gradually takes away Ruch's market share, Kolporter said.
ZYCIE

- International GSM digital mobile phone operators will meet in Warsaw at their first conference in Central and Eastern Europe. Warsaw was chosen as the conference venue as Poland is now the most dynamically developing mobile phone market, Era GSM operator spokeman Robert Niczewski said.
